paper_title: New axion and hidden photon constraints from a solar data global fit
notes: Headline hidden-photon result: solar global fit (helioseismology + solar neutrinos) gives chi*m < 1.8e-12 eV at 3 sigma (Delta chi^2 = 9), from resonant emission of longitudinal hidden photons; this is the 'Sun-L (global)' region in Fig. 11 whose lower boundary is a flat line at chi*m = 1.8e-12 eV. The compilation variable is chi (not chi*m), so I converted chi = 1.8e-12 eV / m along the flat chi*m line. Mass range 3e-5 to 8 eV is the paper's stated range where this constraint is the outermost/most stringent (Fig. 11 and text); the limit physically holds for m <~ 0.3 keV (longitudinal-mode resonant emission). Points lie on the power law chi = 1.8e-12/m and define a straight diagonal in log-log. confidence_level = 0.997 reflects the paper's 3 sigma (Delta chi^2 = 9) upper limit (schema's 0.90/0.95 not applicable). Not a dark-matter search, so no density rescaling (dm_density_assumed null). The paper also reports an axion-photon limit g_agamma < 4.1e-10 GeV^-1 at 3 sigma (g10 < 4.1), but it is explicitly presented as a validation test case that is NOT competitive with CAST/HB; the hidden-photon limit is the paper's novel main result ('most restrictive upper limit available across a wide range of masses').
